section_1.title: Prerequisite Review: The Static Slope
section_1.content: Briefly recall the concept of a 'secant line' slope (rise over run) between two points on a graph. This establishes the baseline for measuring average change.
section_1.example: A hiker climbing a trail between two marker posts: calculating the steepness as a simple ratio of height gain to horizontal distance.

section_2.title: The Concept of Transformation: Secant to Tangent
section_2.content: Animate the process of shrinking the interval between two points. As the second point 'slides' toward the first, the secant line transforms into a tangent line at a single point.
section_2.example: A fast-moving car: imagine taking a photo, then a shorter exposure, until the 'blur' of the path reveals the exact direction the car is pointing at that instant.

section_3.title: Defining the Derivative as a Dynamic Operator
section_3.content: Introduce the derivative not just as a number, but as a 'transformation operator' that turns a function (position) into a new function (velocity/rate of change).
section_3.example: A hungry chameleon extending its tongue: the function maps time to position; the derivative maps time to the 'speed of the strike' at any micro-second.

section_4.title: Visualizing the 'Derivative Function' Graph
section_4.content: Show the original function curve (e.g., a parabola) alongside its derivative curve (e.g., a straight line). Explain how the height of the derivative curve represents the 'slope' of the original at that x-coordinate.
section_4.example: A roller coaster track: The slope of the track at any point determines how fast the coaster feels, visualized as a 'speedometer' graph running parallel to the track.

section_5.title: Summary: The Power of Perspective
section_5.content: Conclude by emphasizing that derivatives allow us to understand global behavior (the whole curve) by examining local transformations (infinitesimal slopes).
section_5.example: Predicting the trajectory of a rocket: By knowing its 'transformational' velocity at every moment, we can determine its exact landing spot.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
